definition: An AI boom is a period of rapid growth in the field of artificial intelligence.
details: The most recent boom happened in the 2020s before seeing increased acceleration and media coverage. Generative AI technologies include large language models (LLM), which generate text and code, image models, and video models, and world models. This period is sometimes referred to as an AI spring, a term used to contrast it with previous AI winters. As of 2026, large frontier models have been released by OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta Superintelligence Labs, and SpaceXAI in the United States, and by the AI industry in China, including Alibaba Cloud, DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, and Z.ai. Many leading models, largely from China, are open weights or open-source; open weights small language models are optimized to run locally on personal computers. These include many models under Alibaba's Qwen, Google's Gemma, Nvidia's Nemotron, and Meta's Muse Glimmer. Key advances preceding precipitating the boom include the transformer (2017), generative pre-trained transformer (2018) and reinforcement learning from human feedback. explainer.lead: An AI boom is a surge in research, investment, products, and public use of artificial intelligence. The current boom began in the mid-2010s and accelerated in the 2020s, bringing generative AI into everyday software while raising concerns about its costs and risks.

tiers.eli5: An AI boom is like a sudden rush to build and use a new kind of tool. Better computer programs learned to write, make pictures, and create other media, so companies invested money and millions of people tried them. This period is also called an AI spring, in contrast to earlier AI winters when progress and excitement slowed.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers work with large language, image, video, and world models, using techniques such as transformers, reasoning models, mixture of experts, and multimodal learning. Open-weight families including Qwen, Gemma, and Nemotron support local or customized deployments, while proprietary models come from major US and Chinese developers. Practical concerns include copyright, security, deepfakes, environmental impact, and hardware supply.
tiers.paperLevel: An AI boom denotes a period of rapid growth in artificial intelligence; the present period began in the mid-2010s and accelerated in the 2020s. Important preceding work includes the transformer in the 2017 paper "Attention Is All You Need", the generative pre-trained transformer in 2018, and reinforcement learning from human feedback. Its scope includes scientific and commercial advances alongside unresolved environmental, economic, security, copyright, and existential risks.

explainer.example: OpenAI launched ChatGPT in November 2022. It gained more than 100 million users in two months, becoming the fastest-growing consumer software application in history and bringing generative AI into public consciousness.

usedIn.name: ChatGPT
usedIn.detail: OpenAI's chatbot popularized general-purpose generative text tasks after launching in November 2022.

usedIn.name: AlphaFold
usedIn.detail: DeepMind's protein-folding system demonstrated a major biomedical advance in 2020.

usedIn.name: DALL-E 2 and Midjourney
usedIn.detail: These 2022 text-to-image systems made image generation widely visible.

usedIn.name: Software development
usedIn.detail: Generative coding tools produce, edit, explain, and debug code.

explainer.intuition: Technical breakthroughs made AI systems much more capable, which attracted users and investment; that growth funded larger models and more products. The boom describes this reinforcing cycle, not one invention or company.
howItWorks: Deep learning and generative models improved machine translation, images, audio, and language.
Transformers, generative pre-training, and human-feedback training enabled more capable systems.
Products such as ChatGPT brought those capabilities to broad public use.
Rising investment and demand expanded model development and AI-capable computing hardware.
Rapid adoption also intensified disputes over safety, copyright, security, and environmental costs.
explainer.whyItMatters: The boom has changed software development, media generation, biomedical research, and the semiconductor industry. Its rapid growth also makes questions about economic concentration, misuse, resource consumption, and long-term risks more urgent.
misconceptions: It did not start with ChatGPT; the current boom began in the mid-2010s and built on earlier advances.
It is not only about chatbots; it also includes image, video, audio, biomedical, and coding systems.
An AI spring does not mean AI has solved every problem or that its risks have disappeared.
